title: Repetition, nesting, randomness and localized structures dominate everywhere

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Repetition, nesting, randomness and localized structures dominate everywhere

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The four themes of repetition, nesting, randomness and localized structures are the dominant types of behavior across a vast range of systems, and these overall behavior types are almost independent of the details of the underlying rules.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 3: The World of Simple Programs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the basic themes of repetition, nesting, randomness and localized structures that we already saw in specific cellular automata in the previous chapter are actually very general, and in fact represent the dominant themes in the behavior of a vast range of different systems.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 3, “The World of Simple Programs”; section “Some Conclusions” (from p. 105), p. 106. Scope: simple programs and, by extension, a vast range of systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch03-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Outputs from many formal systems can be generated, but the central taxonomy and dominance criterion require substantial interpretation. Available surveys cannot adequately cover the claim's open-ended scope or exclude alternative behavior classes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Construct a representative, preregistered sample of formal systems and an independently validated classifier for the four behavior classes, then measure coverage and residual classes. High coverage across sampled families supports a restricted version; frequent unclassified behavior refutes it there.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A vast range has no defined sampling frame.

The taxonomy risks being fitted to the observed outputs.

The four themes are informal and may overlap.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Samples of cellular automata, Turing machines, and related systems can be labeled with Wolfram's four themes using public simulators, and that labeling is informative for those classes. 'Dominant,' 'almost independent of the details,' and the extension to a vast range of systems are loose enough that many outcomes remain compatible with the claim. The test therefore reaches the simple-program core and not the full stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Classify long evolutions of many simple programs into repetition, nesting, apparent randomness, and localized structures, and measure how often a behavior falls outside those four. Dominance of the four classes supports the claim; a large share of a well-defined class falling into a fifth stable type would challenge dominance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The four themes are broad enough that many rival taxonomies can be fitted to the same pictures.

The extension from simple programs to a vast range of systems is not covered by program enumeration alone.
